source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies drift recovery from the Lyapunov covariance equation and states global identifiability exactly for simple graphs, namely graphs without directed two-cycles.
The paper develops a Lyapunov trek expansion, simplifies it for acyclic models, and derives an acyclic marginal-variance lower bound.
The paper studies an l1-regularized estimator for support/model selection from iid equilibrium snapshots and its consistency conditions.
The paper constructs identified-set estimators and confidence regions by inversion of a sample criterion and develops consistency, rates, and inference.
The paper studies inference for directionally differentiable maps, establishes when the ordinary bootstrap fails, and gives an alternative resampling method with local size control.
The paper characterizes weakly regular degree-zero parameters through underlying regular parameters and proves associated impossibility results.
The preprint derives higher-order cumulant equations, generic non-Gaussian drift identification, and an asymptotically distributed semiparametric estimator.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Promote the exact four-sector certificate, rather than the individual slice formulas, as the paper headline and include a compact worked contact instance that evaluates every sector and the strict-attainment decision from covariance primitives.

Derive an explicit finite-dimensional algorithm and operation bound for evaluating the active-set certificate, including dependent-row and equality cases; this would turn the feasibility object into a reproducible decision procedure.
Strengthen the inference contribution with a matching local minimax testing-risk constant or an optimal confidence-set diameter characterization on the stated regular contact subcharts.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with the sector-certificate proof as the load-bearing target, while preserving the explicit contact and local-inference results as the field-tier payoff.
